scheme_name: Goa State Export Market Development Scheme, 2008
description:
The Goa State Export Market Development Scheme was launched in 2008 by the Government of Goa. 

This scheme aims to promote and enhance the export of goods and services from the state of Goa. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to provide financial assistance to small and medium enterprises in Goa to develop their export capabilities. 

The scheme is designed to boost the overall economic development of the state by increasing the export of local products. 

The Goa State Export Market Development Scheme focuses on various sectors including agriculture, fisheries, handicrafts, and manufacturing. 

The government aims to increase the export turnover of Goa-based industries by providing necessary support. 

Under this scheme, financial assistance is provided to eligible exporters for various activities. 

These activities include participation in trade fairs, exhibitions, and buyer-seller meets. 

The scheme also supports the development of marketing strategies and promotional materials for exporters. 

Financial assistance is provided in the form of grants to cover specific expenses incurred by exporters. 

The maximum grant amount available under the scheme is up to 50 percent of the total eligible expenditure. 

The total eligible expenditure is capped at INR 10 lakh for each exporter per financial year. 

This means that an exporter can receive a maximum grant of INR 5 lakh per year. 

The scheme is particularly beneficial for small and medium enterprises that may lack the financial resources to promote their products in international markets. 

Eligibility criteria for the scheme include being a registered small or medium enterprise in Goa. 

The applicant must have a valid export license issued by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade. 

Additionally, the applicant should have a minimum export turnover of INR 5 lakh in the preceding financial year. 

The application process involves submitting a detailed project proposal to the Directorate of Industries, Trade and Commerce, Goa. 

The proposal must outline the intended activities and the estimated budget for the project. 

Applicants are required to provide supporting documents including the export license, financial statements, and a certificate of registration. 

Once the proposal is submitted, it is reviewed by a committee formed by the Directorate of Industries. 

The committee assesses the proposal based on its feasibility and potential impact on exports. 

If approved, the financial assistance is disbursed in a phased manner based on the completion of the proposed activities. 

The scheme operates on a continuous basis with no specific application deadlines. 

However, it is advisable for applicants to submit their proposals well in advance of planned export activities. 

The disbursement of funds typically occurs within three months of approval of the proposal. 

The implementing authority for the Goa State Export Market Development Scheme is the Directorate of Industries, Trade and Commerce, Goa. 

The contact details for the Directorate are as follows: Directorate of Industries, Trade and Commerce, Government of Goa, Panaji, Goa. 

The phone number for inquiries is +91-832-222-3535. 

The email address for communication is ditc.goa@gmail.com. 

The scheme has been instrumental in enhancing the visibility of Goan products in international markets. 

It has facilitated the participation of Goan exporters in various international trade fairs. 

Over the years, the scheme has contributed to an increase in the overall export turnover of Goa. 

In the financial year 2020-2021, Goa's total exports reached approximately INR 5,000 crore. 

This figure represents a significant increase compared to previous years, demonstrating the effectiveness of the scheme. 

The scheme also encourages the development of new products for export. 

It supports innovation and quality improvement in the production processes of Goan industries. 

The government regularly reviews the scheme to ensure it meets the changing needs of exporters. 

Feedback from beneficiaries is taken into account to improve the implementation of the scheme. 

The Goa State Export Market Development Scheme is part of the broader initiative by the Government of India to promote exports. 

The central government has set a target to increase India's exports to USD 1 trillion by 2025. 

The scheme aligns with this national goal by empowering state-level exporters. 

In addition to financial assistance, the scheme also provides advisory support to exporters. 

This includes guidance on market trends, export documentation, and compliance with international standards. 

The Directorate of Industries conducts workshops and training sessions for potential exporters. 

These sessions aim to equip them with the necessary skills and knowledge for successful exporting. 

The scheme has also fostered collaboration between exporters and government agencies. 

This collaboration has led to the identification of new markets for Goan products. 

The government actively promotes the scheme through various channels to reach potential beneficiaries. 

Awareness campaigns are conducted to inform small and medium enterprises about the available support. 

The Goa State Export Market Development Scheme is a vital component of the state's economic strategy. 

It plays a crucial role in enhancing the competitiveness of Goan products in the global market. 

The scheme not only benefits individual exporters but also contributes to job creation in the state. 

By promoting exports, the scheme helps in increasing the income levels of local communities. 

Overall, the Goa State Export Market Development Scheme is a comprehensive initiative aimed at boosting exports. 

It provides essential financial and advisory support to enhance the export capabilities of Goan enterprises. 

The scheme continues to evolve to meet the needs of the changing global market. 

It remains a key driver of economic growth and development in Goa.
